title: How to find your MAC address (Ref: 2992)
content: How to find your MAC address Run 'ipconfig /all' in command prompt to see physical address. Steps: Press Windows Key + R. Type 'cmd' and press Enter. Type 'ipconfig /all' in the terminal. Look for 'Physical Address' under your adapter. Format is XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX.

title: Laptop overheating fixes (Ref: 3252)
content: Laptop overheating fixes Clean dust from vents, ensure fans are spinning, and consider a cooling pad. Steps: Turn off the laptop and let it cool. Use compressed air to blow out dust from vents. Verify that fans are spinning when powered on. Avoid using the laptop on soft surfaces like beds. Apply new thermal paste if you are comfortable disassembling.

title: Upgrading RAM on desktop (Ref: 4928)
content: Upgrading RAM on desktop Ensure you have the correct DDR type. Open the case, unlock slots, and press firmly. Steps: Power off the PC and unplug it. Open the side panel of the case. Locate the RAM slots. Push down the locking tabs. Align the notch on the new RAM stick. Press down firmly until it clicks.

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) common causes (Ref: 6482)
content: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) common causes Driver conflicts, faulty memory, or corrupt system files often cause BSOD. Steps: Note the error code on the blue screen (e.g., MEMORY_MANAGEMENT). Restart the computer. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic tool. Update all device drivers via Device Manager. Run 'sfc /scannow' in Command Prompt.

title: How to troubleshoot startup issues (Ref: 5332)
content: How to troubleshoot startup issues Check power cables, ensure the outlet works, and look for motherboard beeps. Steps: Verify power cable is firmly plugged in. Check if the power outlet is active by testing another device. Listen for any beep codes from the motherboard. Remove any USB drives or peripherals. Press and hold power button for 30 seconds to discharge static.

title: Monitor displays 'No Signal' (Ref: 7859)
content: Monitor displays 'No Signal' Check HDMI/DisplayPort cable connections at both ends. Steps: Ensure monitor power cable is plugged in. Unplug and replug the HDMI/DP cable at both ends. Try a different cable if possible. Verify correct input source (Input button on monitor). Test monitor on another computer.

title: Adjusting color settings (Ref: 3634)
content: Adjusting color settings Use the OSD (On-Screen Display) buttons to change brightness and contrast. Steps: Locate buttons on the monitor (bottom or side). Press Menu to open OSD. Navigate to Picture or Color settings. Adjust Brightness and Contrast to preference. Reset to factory defaults if needed.

title: Dual monitor setup guide (Ref: 2933)
content: Dual monitor setup guide Use 'Extend these displays' in Display Settings for multi-monitor work. Steps: Connect second monitor via free port (HDMI/DP). Right-click desktop and select Display Settings. Scroll to 'Multiple displays'. Select 'Extend these displays' from dropdown. Drag the monitor icons to match physical arrangement.

title: Cleaning your screen (Ref: 1263)
content: Cleaning your screen Use a microfiber cloth and specialized screen cleaner. Do not use Windex. Steps: Turn off the monitor. Wipe gently with a dry microfiber cloth. For stubborn spots, use a specialized screen cleaning spray. Never spray directly on the screen; spray the cloth. Let it dry before turning on.

title: Replacing toner cartridges (Ref: 9815)
content: Replacing toner cartridges Open front panel, pull out old toner, shake new one, and insert until it clicks. Steps: Open the front cover. Grasp the handle of the empty toner. Pull it straight out. Remove packaging from new toner. Shake new toner side-to-side 5 times. Insert until it clicks into place.

title: Dead pixel policy (Ref: 8926)
content: Dead pixel policy We replace monitors with more than 5 bright pixels or 10 dark pixels. Steps: Clean the screen gently to ensure it's not dust. Run a 'dead pixel test' video on YouTube. Count the number of stuck (bright) or dead (black) pixels. Take a photo of the defects. Submit a ticket if count exceeds policy limits.

title: Connecting to network printer (Ref: 3575)
content: Connecting to network printer Use 'Add Printer' in Control Panel and search by IP address. Steps: Go to Control Panel > Devices and Printers. Click 'Add a printer'. Select 'The printer that I want isn't listed'. Choose 'Add a printer using a TCP/IP address'. Enter the printer IP.

title: Paper jam in Tray 2 (Ref: 5961)
content: Paper jam in Tray 2 Open the side door, gently pull the paper out in the direction of feed. Steps: Open Tray 2 and remove loose paper. Open the right side panel. Look for stuck paper. Gently pull paper out; do not tear. Close all doors and restart printer.

title: Printer printing garbage characters (Ref: 7161)
content: Printer printing garbage characters Reinstall the correct driver for your specific model (PCL/PS). Steps: Cancel the print job on the printer. Go to Print Server properties. Remove the current driver. Download universal PCL6 driver from manufacturer site. Install new driver and print test page.

title: Scanned documents not arriving (Ref: 8983)
content: Scanned documents not arriving Check the SMTP settings on the printer console. Steps: Log in to printer web interface. Go to Email/Scan settings. Verify SMTP server address and port (usually 25 or 587). Check 'Test Email' function. Ensure sender email is authorized.

title: Browser keeps crashing (Ref: 9975)
content: Browser keeps crashing Disable recently installed extensions and update the browser. Steps: Open browser menu > Settings. Go to Extensions. Toggle off all extensions. Restart browser. If stable, re-enable extensions one by one.

title: Requesting new software installation (Ref: 2042)
content: Requesting new software installation Submit a ticket with manager approval for paid software. Steps: Check the Approved Software List first. Fill out the 'Software Request' form in GLPI. Attach manager approval email if paid. Wait for IT to assign license. Technician will install remotely.

title: VPN connection errors (Ref: 9893)
content: VPN connection errors Ensure your MFA code is entered correctly and internet is stable. Steps: Check internet connection. Open VPN client (e.g., AnyConnect). Verify server address (vpn.company.com). Enter username and password. Approve MFA notification on phone.

title: Adobe Acrobat Pro license issue (Ref: 7223)
content: Adobe Acrobat Pro license issue Sign out and sign back in to Creative Cloud desktop app. Steps: Open Adobe Creative Cloud app. Click profile icon > Sign Out. Restart the computer. Open Creative Cloud and Sign In. Launch Acrobat Pro.

title: Troubleshooting Office 365 login (Ref: 9523)
content: Troubleshooting Office 365 login Clear browser cache or try Incognito mode if stuck in a loop. Steps: Close all Office apps. Open Word and sign out. Open Control Panel > Credential Manager. Remove all MicrosoftOffice credentials. Reopen Word and sign in again.

title: Router restart procedure (Ref: 3424)
content: Router restart procedure Unplug power for 10 seconds, then replug. Wait 5 minutes for boot. Steps: Locate the power cable on the router. Unplug it from the wall or device. Wait fully 10-30 seconds. Plug it back in. Wait for 'Online' light to turn solid green.

title: Wi-Fi checking signal strength (Ref: 8851)
content: Wi-Fi checking signal strength Use an analyzer tool to check dBm levels in your area. Steps: Click Wi-Fi icon in taskbar. Check number of bars. For detailed check, open CMD. Run 'netsh wlan show interfaces'. Look at 'Signal' percentage.

title: Firewall block request (Ref: 7833)
content: Firewall block request Submit IP details to security team for whitelisting. Steps: Identify the source and destination IP. Clearly state the business justification. Determine the required port (e.g., 443). Fill out Firewall Change Request form. Attach vendor documentation.

title: Access Point flashing red (Ref: 3707)
content: Access Point flashing red Indicates loss of controller connectivity. Check uplink cable. Steps: Trace the ethernet cable from AP. Ensure it's plugged into the wall/switch. Check if switch port has POE. Restart the AP if possible. Report to Network Operations.

title: Transferring calls (Ref: 7832)
content: Transferring calls Press Transfer, dial extension, announce call, then hang up. Steps: While on call, press 'Transfer'. Dial the 4-digit extension. Wait for answer (warm transfer) or hang up (blind). If announcing, say 'Transferring X to you'. Press 'Transfer' again to complete.

title: Resetting desk phone (Ref: 7053)
content: Resetting desk phone Hold # and * while powering on to factory reset. Steps: Unplug ethernet cable (POE). Hold down * and # keys. Plug cable back in while holding keys. Release keys when lights flash text sequence. Phone will format and download config.

title: Conference call guide (Ref: 6043)
content: Conference call guide Dial first party, press Conf, dial second party, press Conf join. Steps: Call the first participant. Press 'Conf' or 'Join'. Dial second number. When they answer, press 'Conf' again. Repeat for additional participants.

title: Headset not working (Ref: 7050)
content: Headset not working Check if headset button is active on base station. Steps: Ensure headset is charged. Check base station power. Press the headset button on the phone. Ensure cable is in the 'Headset' port, not 'Handset'. Adjust volume on the headset itself.

title: Setting up voicemail (Ref: 1255)
content: Setting up voicemail Press the message button and follow voice prompts to set PIN. Steps: Press the 'Envelope' button. Enter temporary PIN (usually 1234). Follow prompts to record name. Record greeting. Set new secure PIN.

title: Laptop battery not charging (Ref: 14709)
content: Laptop battery not charging Battery stuck at 0% or 'Plugged in, not charging' message. Steps: Shut down the laptop. Unplug the AC adapter. If removable, remove the battery. Hold power button for 15 seconds. Reinsert battery and plug in AC adapter.

title: Laptop screen flickering (Ref: 75468)
content: Laptop screen flickering Display flashes on and off or shows artifacts. Steps: Update Graphics Drivers via manufacturer site. Check if the issue happens in BIOS (hardware issue). Reseat the LVDS cable if comfortable opening bezel. Test with an external monitor.

title: Hard Drive noise (Clicking/Grinding) (Ref: 42727)
content: Hard Drive noise (Clicking/Grinding) Unusual sounds indicate mechanical failure. Backup immediately. Steps: Stop using the computer for non-essential tasks. Backup critical data to cloud or external drive immediately. Run 'chkdsk /f' to check for errors. Contact IT for drive replacement. Do not shake or hit the case.

title: Printer offline status (Ref: 45756)
content: Printer offline status Printer shows as Offline in Windows. Steps: Check if printer is powered on and connected to network. Open Devices and Printers > Right click Printer > See what's printing. Uncheck 'Use Printer Offline' in Printer Menu. Restart the Print Spooler service in Services.msc.

title: Streaks or lines on printed pages (Ref: 34115)
content: Streaks or lines on printed pages Dirty drum unit or corona wire. Steps: Remove the drum unit. Clean the corona wire by sliding the tab back and forth. If using inkjet, run 'Clean Printhead' utility. Replace drum if defects persist after cleaning.

title: VPN 'Certificate Validation Failure' (Ref: 53209)
content: VPN 'Certificate Validation Failure' Client certificate missing or expired. Steps: Verify your smart card is inserted (if applicable). Check if your certificates are expired in MMC. Reinstall the VPN client. Contact Security Team for certificate renewal.

title: VPN slows down internet (Ref: 61787)
content: VPN slows down internet Split tunneling might be disabled. Steps: This is often normal as traffic routes through corporate HQ. Disconnect VPN if performing high-bandwidth personal tasks. Use wired connection for better stability.

title: Switch port security violation (Ref: 73200)
content: Switch port security violation Contact network admin to reset port if you changed devices. Steps: Disconnect the unauthorized device. Plug back the original company device. Submit ticket to Network team. Include wall jack number. Wait for port reset confirmation.

title: VPN not working
content: VPN not working Unable to connect to corporate network. Steps: Check if your Wi-Fi is connected. Restart the VPN application. Re-enter your username and password. Restart your computer.

title: Printer not working
content: Printer not working Basic check for non-responsive printer. Steps: Ensure the printer is plugged into power. Check if the green 'Ready' light is on. Make sure there is paper in the tray. Unplug power cord for 30 seconds and plug back in.

title: How to fix VPN issue
content: How to fix VPN issue General steps for common VPN errors. Steps: Disconnect and wait 10 seconds. Click 'Connect' again. Check if you have a valid internet connection (try opening Google). If error persists, contact IT Service Desk.
